newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen mostly steady, instances $0.50 per cwt lower, after another surge in hog marketings on Wednesday, livestock dealers said.
Prices could turn higher, however, as the day progresses amid strong demand from packers who may be planning large Saturday operations, they said.

The projected large Saturday kill was seen as a result of profitable operating margins among packers and a desire to make up lost production at some plants closed Monday in observance of the Easter holiday, dealers said.
One livestock dealer estimated Saturday's slaughter near 80,000 head. Last Saturday's USDA slaughter estimate was revised Monday up 4,000 head to 88,000.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were estimated at $50.50 to $51.00, dealers and packer buyers in that area said and Illinois top prices at the plant were seen at $51.00.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant door could range $50.00 to $50.50, sources there said.
The interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog run on Tuesday totaled 121,000 head, above the estimated 110,000, USDA said. Wednesday's estimate was 110,000 head.
